title: Pre-Existing Condition and Systems Start Terms by Plan — Real Estate Service Contracts
content:
Three plan terms of the Real Estate Service Contracts govern when a buyer-phase failure may be covered with respect to the home's history and the timing of systems coverage.

| Plan | Unknown, undetectable pre-existing conditions covered in the buyer phase | Home inspection completed before closing required for that coverage | Days after closing before systems coverage starts |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bridgewell Closing Starter | No | Yes | 0 (from closing) |
| Bridgewell Closing Standard | Yes | Yes | 0 (from closing) |
| Bridgewell Closing Plus | Yes | Yes | 0 (from closing) |
| Bridgewell Closing Premier | Yes | Yes | 0 (from closing) |
| Bridgewell Closing Premier Two-Year | Yes | Yes | 0 (from closing) |
| Bridgewell New Construction Three-Year | Yes | Yes | 365 |

## What each term is

- **Unknown pre-existing coverage**: whether buyer-phase failures from unknown, undetectable pre-existing conditions are covered.
- **Inspection requirement**: whether that coverage requires a home inspection completed before closing.
- **Systems coverage delay**: the calendar days after closing before heating, cooling, ductwork, plumbing, water heater and electrical coverage starts; 0 means coverage of those systems runs from closing.

## Points of reading

- The Bridgewell Closing Starter plan does not cover unknown, undetectable pre-existing conditions.
- On every plan where that coverage exists, it requires a home inspection completed before closing.
- Only the Bridgewell New Construction Three-Year plan delays systems coverage, by 365 days after closing; the delay applies to heating, cooling, ductwork, plumbing, water heater and electrical coverage.
